$comment: A POLICY DOCUMENT, not a deployed role. Deployment (Phase 18) has not started â€” there is no AWS account, no CDK stack, and nothing here has ever been applied. This file is what infra/ (CDK v2, per CLAUDE.md's repo layout) is expected to synthesize when that phase runs, and what this phase's tests audit against instead of a live role. Resource ARNs use a wildcard account/region segment (':*:*:') because no account exists yet to fill them in; the table name segment is exact and is cross-checked against packages/ledger/src/tables.ts's TABLE_LOGICAL_NAMES by packages/ledger/test/iam-advisory.test.ts, along with a table prefix of 'chaperone' (packages/config's DDB_TABLE_PREFIX default) so a rename of either drifts loudly instead of silently.

roles.name: chaperone-gateway-task-role
roles.description: The instance role for the gateway process itself (docker/gateway.Dockerfile, run on the EC2 host built by infra/lib/ec2-gateway-stack.ts). This is the identity that runs gate.ts, approve.ts, and api.ts, and â€” until the isolated advisory worker (chaperone-model-advisory-role below) is deployed â€” packages/advisory/src/localRunner.ts's putAdvisory/setQuarantineAdvisoryScore calls also execute under this role, not the separate model-scoped one. CLAUDE.md's append-only rule is enforced here at the table-statement level, not just in packages/ledger's client code: the ledger-event statement grants PutItem and read verbs only â€” no UpdateItem, no DeleteItem, no BatchWriteItem â€” so a bug in application code cannot become a write IAM would have allowed anyway.

roles.name: chaperone-model-advisory-role
roles.description: AWS-01: the execution role of the ScoreAdvisory Lambda, the model-calling stage of the Step Functions pipeline (infra/lib/advisory-pipeline-stack.ts, `cdk synth` only, never deployed). The model is openai/gpt-oss-120b, an open-weight model served by Groq, because Bedrock access for this account was declined. It may read ONE Secrets Manager secret (the Groq key, by name, never in the template) and read a quarantine row to build the prompt, and it may do nothing else. No statement names ledger-event, pin, or advisory at all, and the one DynamoDB statement grants only read verbs. There is no PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, or BatchWriteItem anywhere in this role: a compromised or misbehaving model call cannot alter the record a resident is being asked to trust, cannot touch the append-only ledger, cannot re-pin anything, and cannot even write the advisory score it computes (see chaperone-advisory-writer-role, a separate role under a separate Lambda, for that).

roles.name: chaperone-advisory-writer-role
roles.description: AWS-01 (Phase 12/13): the execution role of the WriteAdvisory Lambda, the pipeline's second and final stage â€” infra/lib/advisory-pipeline-stack.ts. Reached only when the Bedrock role above returns a scored result (an 'unavailable' result short-circuits the state machine to Succeed before this Lambda is ever invoked). This role is the mirror image of the Bedrock role: it may PutItem/GetItem on chaperone-advisory only (GetItem for the same idempotent-skip-if-already-scored check packages/advisory/src/localRunner.ts already does), and it has no Bedrock permission, no ledger-event or pin access, and no access to quarantine at all â€” it never re-derives or re-checks anything about the change itself, it only persists a score another role already computed.

roles.name: chaperone-changelog-check-role
roles.description: AWS-01: the execution role of the ChangelogCheck Lambda, the parallel branch that needs no model. It reads a quarantine row (the tool and the day the change was caught) and the pin that quarantine replaces (the day the household approved the old definition), then calls the public GitHub API. GetItem/Query on quarantine and GetItem on pin: no write verb, no secret, no model, no ledger-event.
